summary: Beverwijk charges for on-street parking in two municipal zones, the Centrum (with a Theater sector near the Kennemer Theater, paid until 22:00) and the Beverwijkse Bazaar area (weekends and holidays), at 1.70 euros per hour in 2026 with a free first hour for registered plates in the centre and a 14.30 euro daily maximum there. Policy since late 2023 has widened paid hours, folded the blue zone into paid parking, capped residents at two permits per address and moved to scan-car enforcement from mid-2024, in response to a 2022 survey showing centre occupancy peaking around 78-82 percent on Saturday afternoons and over half of vehicles parked without payment or permit. The NS-owned station park-and-ride at Wijckermolen, used by the municipality's own survey as a spare-capacity site (peak occupancy 6 percent in 2022), has been named in planning papers and a council debate as one possible location for a future built car park, but I found no decision; the Meerplein (448 spaces) is planned for redevelopment from about 2027. The Bazaar runs its own large private car parks with a 5 euro weekend cap, and the municipality is reserving charging bays beside new public charge points and allowing cable charging from home in 2026.

items.text: The Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026 (adopted by the council on 20 November 2025, levy from 1 January 2026) sets on-street tariffs of 1.70 euros per 60 minutes in both Beverwijk Centrum and Beverwijk Bazaar. In Centrum the first 60 minutes cost 0.00 euros when the plate is registered at a machine or by phone; the daily maximum is 14.30 euros in Centrum, there is no daily maximum at the Bazaar, and the penalty is 82.00 euros.

The Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2025 set 1.65 euros per hour from the second hour in Centrum and at the Bazaar, a free first hour in Centrum, a 14.00 euro daily maximum in Centrum and 27.86 euros for a first resident permit. The 2026 ordinance therefore raised the hourly rate by 0.05 euros, the daily maximum by 0.30 euros and the first resident permit to 28.47 euros.

The Aanwijsbesluit parkeren 2025 (Gemeenteblad of 6 January 2025) sets paid hours in Beverwijk Centrum at Monday to Saturday 09:00-19:00, in the Theater sector around the Kennemer Theater at Monday to Saturday 09:00-22:00, and at the Bazaar on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays 07:00-18:00. It lists the street Wijckermolen in the paid Centrum zone; I found no 2026 replacement decision, so this 2025 list is the latest I read.

The Nadere regels parkeren 2025 allow at most two resident permits per registered address in the centre and a visitor bundle of 200 hours a year in Centrum and 260 hours in the Theater sector for the same price. Residents of new-build projects in the Stadskant Spoorzone, where parking is arranged on private land, are excluded from resident and visitor permits. The 2026 tariff table prices the 1st and 2nd resident permit at 28.47 and 91.12 euros and visitor hours at 0.27 euros per hour in Centrum.
items.source_title: Nadere regels parkeren 2025, Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 1720 (and Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026)

items.text: The council adopted the Nota Parkeernormen en Afkoopregeling Parkeren 2024 on 12 October 2023, in force from 1 November 2023: the exemption for small developments (kruimelregeling) was dropped, a specific part of the Stadskant Spoorzone gets lower parking norms for new housing, and buy-out contributions are indexed by 2 percent a year. Using spare capacity in the centre costs developers 5,000 euros per space.
items.source_title: Nota Parkeernormen en Afkoopregeling Parkeren 2024, Gemeenteblad 2023 nr. 462890

items.text: On 28 September 2023 five council parties (D66, Samen Lokaal, PvdA, GroenLinks, O'ns Beverwijk) tabled an amendment asking that centre paid parking be extended to 19:00 on weekdays, introduced on Saturdays 09:00-19:00, extended to 22:00 around the Kennemer Theater, that the centre zones including the blue zone be merged, and that residents get at most two permits per address. The 2025 designation decision later shows these hours in force.
items.source_title: Amendement Nota Parkeernormen en Afkoopregeling parkeren 2024 / Verordening Parkeerbelasting 2024 (D-102156)

items.text: A 2022 survey reported to the council on 6 April 2023 found the busiest centre moment was Saturday 14:00-16:00 at 78 percent average occupancy (Thursday evening 72 percent), against the council's 85 percent maximum. Of all parked vehicles, 52 percent had neither a permit nor paid, 80 percent on the Meerplein and over 95 percent on the Breestraat. Centre-wide Saturday-afternoon occupancy for 2019-2022 was 78, 80, 84 and 82 percent.

In the same 2022 survey the NS park-and-ride at the station peaked at only 6 percent occupancy, and at 2 percent at the busiest centre moment on Saturday (non-rail users pay there while centre parking was free on Saturdays); it was 8 percent full during the June 2022 city festival. Around the Meerplein the lots had about 225 spare places at the Saturday peak (125 without the P+R).

The edge car parks behaved unevenly in 2022: Wijckerpoort averaged 23 percent but reached 98 percent on Thursday afternoon, and Halve Maan averaged 57 percent with a 95 percent peak on Thursday evening. The memo also reported that the Meerplein was busiest on market-day Wednesday at 67 percent, with about 80 spare places.

The college's proposal 'verbetervoorstellen parkeerbeleid 2025' of 24 September 2024 suggested a 17.00 euro daily maximum (uncapped days would cost 24.50 euros in Centrum and 33.65 in the Theater zone) and a free first hour Monday to Saturday as its preferred scenario. It noted that under 6 percent of transactions last over 4 hours and that the parking fund would only break even from 2026; the ordinances finally published set different maxima (14.00 euros for 2025, 14.30 for 2026).

The same September 2024 proposal asked for 94,053 euros to add 9 and move 3 pay machines in the centre, and planned information columns at the car parks Halve Maan, Beverplein, Meerplein and Wijckerpoort able to take a future parking guidance system, whose feasibility per car park was to be studied in 2025. It also flagged that a possible built car park would be harder to operate if more free parking were allowed.

Beverwijk began testing a licence-plate scan car on 23 May 2024 in the paid zones Centrum, Theater sector and Bazaar, with no fines during the test, checking plates against the national parking register (NPR) and sending hits to an enforcement officer. Official use in the centre was planned from 25 June 2024 after a successful evaluation.
items.source_title: Persbericht Beverwijk start test met scanauto voor parkeercontrole (D-122762)

items.text: A consultancy note for the municipality (Iv-Infra, 22 August 2023) said the NS park-and-ride at Wijckermolen was barely used, that the municipality was talking to the site owner NS, and that it was a search location, with the Meerplein, Halve Maan and Wijckerpoort, for a future stacked car park. It assumed the 75 spaces at the Slangenwegje would go around 2024-2025 and the 448 public Meerplein spaces from about 2027; this is a planning assumption, not a decision.
items.source_title: Notitie maatregelen met betrekking tot parkeren in het centrum van Beverwijk (Iv-Infra, INFR230340)

items.text: At the council committee of 21 September 2023 the party Samen Lokaal said it wanted an above-ground car park near the centre, naming the NS park-and-ride as a possible site, and several other speakers said they favoured a car park if affordable. These are party positions in a debate, and the 2024 follow-up proposal I found did not contain a decision on a car park.

By decisions dated 4 June 2026 (Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 254133 and a car park decision for Plantage nr. 270481; a further one dated 22 June 2026, nr. 297218) the college reserves two parking spaces next to each public charge point for charging only, using sign E8c. The 4 June collective decision says the charge point must be built within three years.
items.source_title: Verzameld verkeersbesluit reserveren parkeerplaatsen voor opladen elektrische voertuigen, Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 254133

items.text: The college's Nadere regels for extended private charging (decision referred to as 6 January 2026, under the 2026 Algemene Plaatselijke Verordening adopted on 18 December 2025) allow residents without private parking to run a charge cable of at most 5 metres over the pavement to a public parking space, between 20:00 and 16:00, without a notification duty. I did not confirm the publication date on the page.
items.source_title: Nadere regels gebruik openbare weg voor het verlengde private laden, Gemeenteblad 2026 nr. 186298

items.text: The Beverwijkse Bazaar runs its own signed car parks P0, P1, P3, P4 and P5; the Bazaar's visitor page, read on 21 October 2026 and undated, states weekend parking costs at most 5 euros per car per day (4.50 euros pre-bought online), Friday is free unless there is an event, there is camera supervision and 16 charge points on P4. The page gives no capacity figures; separately the municipal on-street Bazaar zone is charged at 1.70 euros per hour.
items.source_title: Openingstijden, Route & Parkeren, De Bazaar Beverwijk

items.text: An undated Noord-Holland provincial annex on free and paid park-and-ride, read on 21 October 2026, names P+R Beverwijk among the sites using the 'NS/Q-Park method': a reduced daily rate (0 to 8 euros depending on site) if the user can show a train journey checked in and out with an OV-chipkaart. It only names the site in a caption, so the Beverwijk-specific tariff and operator are not confirmed here.
items.source_title: Bijlage 12 Gratis en betaald parkeren, Provincie Noord-Holland

gaps: https://www.beverwijk.nl (all pages incl. /parkeren, /scanauto, /parkeernormen): the municipal site showed a 'temporarily unavailable, security precaution' page on 21 October 2026, so current tariffs, zone maps and park-and-ride information could not be read there
https://www.rodi.nl/beverwijk/nieuws/354088/college-b-en-w-stemt-in-met-aangescherpt-parkeerbeleid and the other rodi.nl local-news pages: returned 'Toegang geweigerd' (blocked), not worked around
No 2026 Aanwijsbesluit parkeren (paid hours and street list) found; the 2025 decision (Gemeenteblad 2025 nr. 4164) was the latest read, so 2026 hours are not confirmed

No Beverwijk document found on the status of a built car park (Meerplein, Halve Maan, Wijckerpoort, NS P+R), on the 2025 'Nota Parkeernormen 2025', on the end-2025 cost-covering parking proposal, or on a parking guidance system; the Meerplein 2027 redevelopment date is from a 2023 consultancy note only

Station P+R Wijckermolen (121 spaces, NS-owned, operator reportedly Q-Park): no primary NS or Q-Park page with current tariff or capacity could be opened (q-park.nl and ns.nl station pages returned 404 or empty); the third-party listing centrumparkeren.nl was not used as support
Bazaar on-street and private car park capacity and visitor numbers: no figures found; the traffic/bereikbaarheid plan for the Bazaar was not found

EV charging: the locations annexes (Bijlage 1 'Lijst laadlocaties') of the June 2026 traffic decisions are separate files not read, and no municipal charging strategy (laadvisie) or charge-point count was opened
Utilisation statements newer than the November 2022 survey (e.g. the spring 2024 parking-pressure measurements and the Deelevaluatie memo D-128637) were not found
Scan-car outcome since mid-2024 (fines, evaluation): no Beverwijk source found
